code.originalText: Three-month diabetes, blood pressure, and eye pressure review

text.paragraph: Three-month diabetes, blood pressure, and eye pressure review. [S]

Mr. Cash returns for his three-month review, nine weeks after sitagliptin and midodrine 2.5 mg were started and five weeks after his annual wellness visit. His fasting home readings now run 120 to 150 mg/dL, with none below 70. He is less lightheaded than before midodrine, but he still feels faint for a minute or two after getting up in the morning and after lunch, and he has had no falls. He takes the last midodrine by mid-afternoon and has no scalp tingling or trouble passing urine. He has started physical therapy for gait and balance, and the low-vision home visit is booked. He uses both eye drops every day without stinging. No eye pressure check was done between visits. He is writing and recording at home. [S]

list.item:
Neurogenic orthostatic hypotension (I95.1). Standing systolic pressure 114 mmHg on midodrine 2.5 mg, with symptoms after rising and after meals. Lying pressure 146/82 mmHg leaves room to raise the dose. [S]
Increase midodrine to 5 mg on waking, at midday, and mid-afternoon, with the last dose at least four hours before bed.
Smaller, lower-carbohydrate lunches to reduce the fall in pressure after meals.
Lying, seated, and standing pressure at the six-month review.

Type 2 diabetes with diabetic autonomic neuropathy (E11.43). HbA1c 7.7%, down from 8.6% and close to his goal below 7.5%, with no hypoglycemia. [S]
Continue metformin and sitagliptin.
HbA1c at the six-month review.

Hyperlipidemia (E78.5). LDL 74 mg/dL, down from 128 on atorvastatin 40 mg. That is a 42 percent fall, short of the 50 percent expected on a high-intensity dose and just above the goal below 70. He reports taking it every day. ALT 27 U/L, normal. [S]
Continue atorvastatin 40 mg and reinforce daily use.
Add ezetimibe if LDL is still 70 or more at the annual review.
Lipid panel at the annual review.

Primary open-angle glaucoma, severe stage (H40.1133). Eye pressures 15 and 16 mmHg, down from 22 and 24, meet the eye clinic's target of 16 or less. Neither drop lowers blood pressure or heart rate. [S]
Continue latanoprost and dorzolamide.
OCT and visual fields at six months with the eye clinic.

Immunization and preventive care. PCV20 was given at the first visit; recombinant zoster vaccine was planned for today. [S]
Recombinant zoster vaccine dose 1 given today; dose 2 in two to six months.
Hepatitis C antibody drawn with today's tests, as planned at the wellness visit.
